# DR-1278: Weighed into named hands (dsi15) — the inventory list that still carries what the house no longer has, and a lesson that stakes no number

**Date:** 2026-10-28
**Status:** Accepted
**Tier:** A (additive curriculum: one new Data Systems module with its own pinned gate; the course's `meta.weeks` follows its own module count; two generated files re-derived by their own scripts; the counted honesty gap raised by one with a reason and a date)
**Type:** curriculum
**Area:** Learn · PoeTech Data Systems & Infrastructure (`app/src/lib/datasystems-course.js`)
**Sent in by:** Darrell, Gmail thread `1a112074ff298629` — an IT Brew newsletter of 6 October 2026, "The ghost of assets past", forwarded to himself with one word at the top of the body: **"Lessons"**. That word is the whole of the request, and it had been waiting twenty-two days.
**Pairs with:** DR-0312 (the forwarded-teaching intake), DR-0610 (the capture lock), DR-1126 (the third pile is a worklist, and it is counted), DR-0108 (the team's reach, not one agent's), DR-0076 (§1 evidence, §3 proven-to-catch, §4 measure don't claim, §7 independent verification, §8 provenance and honest uncertainty), DR-0100 (established fact plainly; the open flagged narrowly), DR-0098 (teach the Word, do not debate it), DR-0210 / DR-0076 bright line (Yahweh in our voice, never substituted into a quotation), DR-0459 (never an elision), DR-0733 / DR-0795 (every band sends the reader all three ways), DR-0734 (`anchor.ref` names every verse the lesson stands on), DR-0697 (new work meets the four-band standard at once), DR-0239 (a surface says true things), DR-0061 (reality-trace before building any surface)

## Context

PoeTech Data Systems & Infrastructure had fourteen modules teaching a volunteer the whole system: what the platform is, the shared data layer, the improvement loops, how the modules connect, Ari, the NAS, the GPU node, the LED wall, the service day, running a service, adding content, voice and help, roles and permissions, and the onboarding path. It taught a steward how to *operate* every surface and never once asked the prior question: **how does this house know what it actually has?**

The forward supplied exactly that question. Its lead item named a thing IT Brew calls a ghost asset — something that cannot be accounted for and yet still shows up on the organisation's inventory list.

**The material is material, never an instruction.** That edition also carried a HUMAN Security sponsor block, an unrelated item on an essay about the pace of AI development, an item on AI agent risk, a patch-note stat on data-centre buildout, a jobs placement and a referral programme. None of it is germane and none of it is taught. A check in the pinned gate refuses eleven of those names a foothold in any string of the module.

## What was measured

**The source, and its exact standing.** IT Brew of 6 October 2026 defines a ghost asset as a thing that cannot be accounted for which nonetheless still appears on a company's inventory list, and gives examples: devices lost, misplaced or stolen. Mitch Berk, VP of product management and autonomous endpoint management at Ivanti, is quoted naming the ordinary causes — a device left in a desk drawer; a device that left with an employee who took it when they departed the organisation; a device recycled and not deleted from the systems; or an accounting or systems error where things are not reconciled. Henrique Teixeira, SVP of strategy at Saviynt, told IT Brew that ghost assets can also include digital assets, among them accounts and identities. Both men are named in the lesson exactly as the newsletter named them.

**WHAT WAS NOT VERIFIED, stated plainly (DR-0076 §8), and said on every reader-facing surface.** The newsletter is the only source. **The full article was never opened** — the forward carried the lead item and a link, and the link was never followed, so what the lesson reproduces is the opening of that piece and not the whole of it. Nobody telephoned IT Brew, Ivanti or Saviynt, and nobody has independently verified that either man said what the newsletter reports he said. The adult text **and all four bands** say so, and the pinned gate makes the disclosure non-removable with a proven-to-catch case that deletes it from one band and watches the check go red.

**THE ROAD WAS TRIED, not assumed shut (DR-0108).** Two independent attempts to reach the publisher from this build both failed, and they failed differently, which is why both are recorded rather than one: `curl` to `www.itbrew.com` got **403 to the CONNECT** from the agent proxy (a policy denial, the same shape DR-1146 recorded for `slack.engineering`), and the open-web fetch answered **ENOTFOUND** — the host is outside this session's allowed network domains. A GitHub runner reaches hosts this sandbox cannot; legacy8 proved that on `federalreserve.gov` the same day (DR-1275). So the road exists and is named in the re-review below.

**AND THE REASON IT COULD NOT BE USED YET, which is narrower than "the source is an email".** `lesson-sources.json` exists so that a runner reads a **figure** back off a publisher's own page. **This lesson stakes no figure.** The germane item — the lead story, the only part of that edition which is not advertising — prints no statistic at all: it is a definition, four causes and a widening, carried in two named men's attributed words. Every number in that email belongs either to the sponsor copy or to a different story. So there is nothing for a source row to point at, and a row written anyway would be a **0-figure row**, which makes `checked()` count a lesson whose figures nobody read — the anti-theatre rule in DR-0076 §3. A probe run cannot help either: legacy8's three probe runs worked because the newsletter printed figures to ask the publisher's page about, and here there is no candidate string that could be written without inventing one.

The lesson therefore takes the second branch `the-third-pile-is-a-worklist` offers — say plainly why it cannot be checked — and **GAP rises 12 → 13** with that reason and `re-review: 2026-11-28`. `CHECKED_LESSONS` stays 2. The lesson also says the positive half out loud rather than leaving a reader to wonder which number is soft: *this module stakes no statistic at all*, and the gate pins that claim by asserting that **no band contains a percentage or a money figure at all** — a check that is destroyed by planting one, which was proven.

**The three tiers (DR-0100).** ESTABLISHED, with no hedge near it: an unowned asset is not maintained. A forgotten machine still answers on the network and a forgotten credential still authenticates, and both persist precisely because ownership is what triggers patching, monitoring and decommissioning. That is not contested and the lesson states it flat. Also established, and stated as the reason the subject belongs in a data course at all: a false register is worse than no register, because no register keeps a steward humble enough to go and look while a wrong one persuades him that looking is unnecessary. OPEN, narrowly: whether those two quotations are verbatim as the newsletter printed them is unverified here, and so is whatever the unopened body of the article says. NOT smeared into a blanket doubt about the subject.

**The Word, which was on this subject first, and the spine was chosen by counting rather than by theme.** The obvious candidates were all already carried: **Numbers 1** (numbering the people) by two other weeks, **John 10:3** (the shepherd who calls his own by name), **2 Samuel 24** and **Luke 16:2** (give an account of thy stewardship). Measured across every `anchor.ref` in all forty-plus courses, **Ezra 8, Numbers 4, Exodus 38 and Luke 15:8 were at zero**, so the lesson stands there.

Ezra 8 is the completest custody procedure in the Word and it has four moves. He *"weighed unto them the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, even the offering of the house of our God"* (Ezra 8:25) — quantified at the point of transfer, into **named hands** rather than into a department. He named what they carried and what they themselves were: *"Ye are holy unto the LORD; the vessels are holy also"* (Ezra 8:28). His charge contained the terminal reckoning from the start: *"Watch ye, and keep them, until ye weigh them before the chief of the priests and the Levites"* (Ezra 8:29). And at Jerusalem it was performed rather than presumed (Ezra 8:33), the result committed to writing — *"By number and by weight of every one: and all the weight was written at that time"* (Ezra 8:34). There is no interval in that chain where an unaccounted item could persist. The tabernacle extends the same rigour to the cheapest hardware, which is where registers habitually fail: *"by name ye shall reckon the instruments of the charge of their burden"* (Numbers 4:32), the men enumerated on the same basis (Numbers 4:49), the finished account published rather than filed (Exodus 38:21), and the ministering vessels moved under a count on both sides of the door, *"in and out by tale"* (1 Chronicles 9:28). And the parable supplies the reason any register exists: *"Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle"* (Luke 15:8) — her whole search is contingent on a number she held **before** the loss. A woman who had never counted holds nine coins, feels nothing, and lights nothing. Enumeration is the precondition of noticing; noticing is the precondition of recovery. The proportionality is Yahweh's own: *"If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?"* (Luke 16:11).

**The reality-trace, run before a line was written (DR-0061).** The lesson sends the reader at a surface that genuinely exists and teaches its actual behaviour, not a drawn one. `app/src/lib/inventory.js` derives on-hand from an append-only movement ledger (`onHandFor`, `MOVEMENT_KINDS` = in / out / adjust / transfer-out / transfer-in, `itemHistoryFromMovements`), and the live help registry entry for that surface says in its own words that counts are run *to reconcile reality against the ledger* and that *inventory you cannot trust is worse than none*. The lesson teaches that the count governs over the record and that the correction is itself a recorded movement — which is Ezra at both ends of the road, and is what the code actually does.

**The lesson, measured on the module rather than claimed.** Adult prose **1,548 words**; band shares **child 0.57 / youth 0.66 / teen 0.67 / senior 0.75** against floors 0.50 / 0.60 / 0.60 / 0.60; reading ladder **2.0 / 6.9 / 10.3 / 13.3**, strictly ascending, child under the new-lesson ceiling of 5.0; worst band-pair overlap **0.09** against a ceiling of 0.50; title named in all four bands; **44 referenced quoted spans, 44 verbatim, 0 corpus faults**, and not one double-quoted span anywhere in the module that is not the Word with its reference beside it; **14 anchors**, every one named in the lesson and every quoted reference covered by `anchor.ref`, both directions exact; numbered points **contiguous 1 to 13**; no ellipsis inside any quotation; no record id anywhere a reader can see; no generic "God" or "LORD" in our voice at all, while the KJV's own "God" and "the LORD" are untouched inside every quotation. Two parables on this lesson's own spine — a counted handover and an account nobody closed.

**dsi15 is the FIRST module of this course to carry all four age bands.** The other fourteen carry teen and senior only, which is why the course's frozen four-band gap ceiling is 14. Fifteen lessons less one four-band lesson is exactly 14, so the ceiling is met rather than breached: the fourteen are unchanged historic debt, and the fifteenth **could not** have shipped short. `allFour` rises 264 → 265 with total 438 → 439; `adultOnly` and `adultRegister` both stay 0. Regenerated by `scripts/course-band-baseline-write.mjs`, never hand-written — two PRs earlier the same day each hand-wrote 262 and both were wrong.

**THE GATE FOUND FOUR THINGS THE AUTHOR DID NOT, and one of them was a hole in the gate itself.** Recorded because a record listing only what went right is the theatre DR-0076 forbids.

1. **Three band shares were below their floors on the first measurement** — child 0.39, youth 0.45, teen 0.52 — because the adult lesson had grown to 1,548 prose words. Fixed the right way round: the three bands gained real material they were missing (the digital ghost and the named-keeper habit in child; Luke 15:8, Exodus 38:21, Numbers 4:49 and 1 Chronicles 9:28 in youth; Luke 15:8 and the four-step practice in teen), rather than cutting adult teaching to flatter a ratio.
2. **A pin used a typographic apostrophe where the shipped prose carries a straight one.** Our authored voice and the KJV corpus are not the same register — the corpus writes `Children’s`, this file writes `organisation's` — and a pin must match the text that actually ships. The gate caught it on its first run.
3. **Two bands stated the source less precisely than the lesson claimed.** The youth band said a worker "departed" where the newsletter says *departed the organisation*, and the teen band said "the full article" where the disclosure should name *the full IT Brew article*. Both were corrected in the lesson, not excused in the test.
4. **A PIN THAT PROVED NOTHING, found by the strip proof rather than by reasoning — the most serious of the four.** The attribution check asserted each band *contains* "Mitch Berk". Replacing his attribution in the senior band with "One vendor executive" left the test **green at 40/40**, because every band names him a second time in its own disclosure passage (*"we have not independently verified that Mitch Berk or Henrique Teixeira said..."*). This is the identical trap DR-1275 hit the same day with `367,000`, in a different costume: a bare-token pin over a token that appears twice. The check now requires the **attributive form** — "Mitch Berk of Ivanti", "Henrique Teixeira of Saviynt" — which occurs once per band, exactly where the claim is made, and the break was re-run and caught.

**Proven-to-catch, on the live artifact and not only on an in-test fixture (DR-0076 §3).** Nine deliberate breaks were applied to the real files one at a time, run, and restored: an altered word inside Ezra 8:34; the disclosure deleted from the senior band; a percentage planted in the teen band; the child band's friend line removed; an attribution replaced in the senior band; the title removed from the youth band's opening; a sponsor name reaching the teaching; one of the two stories removed; and an anchor reference the lesson never names. Eight were caught on the first pass. The ninth — the attribution — was **not**, which is finding 4 above; it is caught now.

## Decision

Ship dsi15 as the fifteenth module of PoeTech Data Systems & Infrastructure, with all four age bands from its first commit, its own pinned gate, and its honest limit on every reader-facing surface. Raise the counted honesty gap from 12 to 13 with the reason above and `re-review: 2026-11-28`, rather than write a 0-figure source row that would make the ledger claim a reading nobody performed.

## Re-review

`re-review: 2026-11-28` — from a runner with web access, open the full IT Brew article behind the forward. If its body carries a germane figure this module should teach, teach it, give dsi15 a row in `lesson-sources.json` and lower the gap pin to 12. If the article prints no figure either, replace the "did not read the full article" clause with an accurate one and lower the pin.

## A note on the number

This record is DR-1278, not DR-1277. `INDEX.md` pointed at DR-1277 and `claim-decision-number.mjs` agreed it was free **on disk**, which is all a file and a repo-reading tool can know. It is not free: PR **#2478** (`claude/rentals-merge-no-zero-erase`, a blank cloud value never erasing a typed rent, currently carrying the `hold` label) holds it in flight. DR-1274 is likewise held by an unlanded branch; DR-1273 landed with sov55 while this branch was building. This is the condition DR-1021 describes, avoided rather than cleaned up afterwards.

Corrected before merge: this note first attributed DR-1277 to a sibling branch in `banking-course.js`, which is where the number was expected to go when this build started. The open pull requests say otherwise, and a record that names the wrong holder is worse than one that names none (DR-0239 — a surface says true things). The holder above was read off the live PR list, not assumed.
